def-locally-lipschitz-ito-sde-and-maxima:
## Definition

Assume AC. Fix a finite horizon $T>0$, finite dimensions $d,m\ge1$, and an
open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$. Use a complete usual filtered probability
space and an adapted standard $m$-dimensional Brownian motion whose increments
after time $s$ are independent of $\mathcal F_s$, as in
[[def-d-dimensional-brownian-motion]] and
[[def-continuous-brownian-ito-process]]. Let $b:[0,T]\times U\to\mathbb R^d$
and $\sigma:[0,T]\times U\to\mathbb R^{d\times m}$ be Borel maps. Require
that they are bounded on every compact subset of $[0,T]\times U$ and locally
Lipschitz in the state uniformly in time: for every compact $K\subset U$ there
is $L_K<\infty$ such that, for every $t\in[0,T]$ and $x,y\in K$,
$$|b(t,x)-b(t,y)|+\|\sigma(t,x)-\sigma(t,y)\|_F\le L_K|x-y|.$$
Let $\xi$ be $\mathcal F_0$-measurable, take values in $U$ almost surely, be
independent of the future Brownian increments, and satisfy $\mathbb E|\xi|^2<\infty$.

For $n\ge1$, set
$$K_n=\{x\in U: |x|\le n,\ \operatorname{dist}(x,U^c)\ge n^{-1}\}.$$
When $U=\mathbb R^d$, interpret $\operatorname{dist}(x,U^c)=+\infty$.
The compact sets $K_n$ are nested and their interiors exhaust $U$. A **local
strong solution up to exit** is the compatible family of stopped adapted
continuous processes $X^{(n)}$ and stopping times $\tau_n$ such that
$$\tau_n=\inf\{t\in[0,T]:X^{(n)}_t\notin\operatorname{int}K_n\}\wedge T, \qquad X^{(n)}_{t\wedge\tau_n}=\xi+\int_0^{t\wedge\tau_n}b(s,X^{(n)}_s)\,ds+ \int_0^{t\wedge\tau_n}\sigma(s,X^{(n)}_s)\,dW_s,$$
with the equation holding indistinguishably and with $X^{(n)}$ constant after
$\tau_n$. Empty early $K_n$ simply give $\tau_n=0$. Compatibility means that
for $m\ge n$, $X^{(m)}$ stopped at $\tau_n$ equals $X^{(n)}$ up to
indistinguishability. The maximal lifetime is $\zeta=\lim_n\tau_n$; for
$t<\zeta$, the common value of $X^{(n)}_t$ for sufficiently large $n$ defines
the maximal local solution $X_t$.

This definition records a local integral equation; it does not assert that a
solution exists or that $\zeta=T$. Those are separate theorem obligations.
The local coefficient conditions allow superlinear growth; global Lipschitz
hypotheses will be imposed only on the coefficient truncations used in the
existence proof.
lem-brownian-ito-integral-bdg-moment-bou:
## Statement

Assume AC and the usual filtered Brownian conventions of
[[def-continuous-brownian-ito-process]]. Let $G$ be a predictable
$d\times m$ matrix process on $[0,T]$ with
$$\mathbb E\left(\int_0^T\|G_s\|_F^2\,ds\right)^{p/2}<\infty$$
for some real $p\ge2$, and let $M_t=\int_0^tG_s\,dW_s$ be its continuous
vector Itô integral. There is a finite constant $C_{p,d}$, independent of
$G$ and $T$, such that
$$\mathbb E\sup_{0\le t\le T}|M_t|^p\le C_{p,d}\, \mathbb E\left(\int_0^T\|G_s\|_F^2\,ds\right)^{p/2}.$$
alg-cir-lamperti-positive-implicit-schem:
## Definition

Assume AC and the Brownian conventions of
[[def-locally-lipschitz-ito-sde-and-maximal-solution]] on $[0,T]$ with
$U=(0,\infty)$. The input consists of $\kappa,\theta,\sigma>0$ satisfying
the Feller condition $2\kappa\theta\ge\sigma^2$, a step $h>0$, a current
transformed value $z_n\ge0$, and a finite Brownian increment $\Delta W_n$.
Set
$$a=\frac{4\kappa\theta-\sigma^2}{8},\qquad A=1+\frac{\kappa h}{2},\qquad c=z_n+\frac{\sigma}{2}\Delta W_n.$$
For valid parameters, $a>0$ and $A>0$. Compute
$$z_{n+1}=\frac{c+\sqrt{c^2+4Aah}}{2A},\qquad x_{n+1}=z_{n+1}^2.$$
This is the positive-root solution of
$$A z_{n+1}^2-cz_{n+1}-ah=0,$$
which is the drift-implicit Euler equation for the Lamperti variable
$Z=\sqrt X$ in the CIR model
$dX_t=\kappa(\theta-X_t)dt+\sigma\sqrt{X_t}\,dW_t$.

Return `invalid-input` for parameters outside the stated domain or a
non-finite input. Otherwise return `success` with $(z_{n+1},x_{n+1})$. In
exact real arithmetic the discriminant is strictly positive and the displayed
root is finite and positive for every $z_n\ge0$ and $\Delta W_n\in\mathbb R$;
the algorithm has no rejected root branch. A floating-point implementation
that cannot verify a finite positive root returns `solve-failure` and does
not advance the state. This is a specific implicit square-root update, not
the ordinary Euler–Maruyama update for $X$.
alg-tamed-euler-superlinear-drift:
## Definition

Assume AC and the Brownian conventions of
[[def-locally-lipschitz-ito-sde-and-maximal-solution]] on $[0,T]$ with
$U=\mathbb R^d$. The input is an autonomous drift $b:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb
R^d$, diffusion $\sigma:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times m}$, initial state
$\xi$, and integer $N\ge1$ with $h=T/N\le1$. Define $t_n=nh$ and
$$b_h(x)=\frac{b(x)}{1+h|b(x)|}.$$
Return the grid values, step process, continuous interpolation, and status as
follows.

1. Set $Y_0=\xi$.
2. For $n=0,\ldots,N-1$, set $\Delta W_n=W_{t_{n+1}}-W_{t_n}$ and
$$Y_{n+1}=Y_n+h b_h(Y_n)+\sigma(Y_n)\Delta W_n.$$
3. Set $\bar Y_t=Y_n$ on $[t_n,t_{n+1})$, with $\bar Y_T=Y_N$, and set
$$Y_t=Y_n+(t-t_n)b_h(Y_n)+\sigma(Y_n)(W_t-W_{t_n}), \qquad t\in[t_n,t_{n+1}].$$
The shared endpoint formulas agree with the grid recursion.

If the dimensions, horizon, step count, or finite-valued coefficient inputs
are invalid, return `invalid-input` without a trajectory. Otherwise return
`success` and the sequence. In exact real arithmetic each update is a finite
vector expression, and $|h b_h(x)|\le1$, so the finite recursion has no
implicit solve or branch failure. The algorithm by itself asserts no moment,
stability, or convergence property.
thm-local-sde-existence-and-uniqueness-u:
## Statement

Assume the data of [[def-locally-lipschitz-ito-sde-and-maximal-solution]] on
$[0,T]$, with $\mathbb E|\xi|^2<\infty$. Then a local strong solution up to
the exit time from $U$ exists on the given filtered space. It is unique up to
indistinguishability before its maximal lifetime $\zeta=\lim_n\tau_n$.
Equivalently, its stopped solutions on the compact exhaustion $K_n$ form a
compatible family as defined in that item. This theorem does not assert that
$\zeta=T$; a separate non-explosion argument is required.
lem-cir-lamperti-transform-and-positive-:
## Statement

Let $\kappa,\theta,\sigma>0$ satisfy the Feller condition
$2\kappa\theta\ge\sigma^2$, and put
$$a=\frac{4\kappa\theta-\sigma^2}{8}.$$
For a positive local strong solution of the CIR SDE
$$dX_t=\kappa(\theta-X_t)dt+\sigma\sqrt{X_t}\,dW_t$$
on $U=(0,\infty)$, the Lamperti variable $Z_t=\sqrt{X_t}$ satisfies
$$dZ_t=\left(\frac a{Z_t}-\frac\kappa2 Z_t\right)dt+ \frac\sigma2dW_t$$
up to every compact exit time. Moreover, for every $h>0$, $z\ge0$, and
$\Delta W\in\mathbb R$, the drift-implicit step
$$z_+=z+h\left(\frac a{z_+}-\frac\kappa2z_+\right) +\frac\sigma2\Delta W$$
has exactly one positive root. It is the value defined by
[[alg-cir-lamperti-positive-implicit-scheme]]. The boundary input $z=0$ is
included for the numerical root statement; the CIR solution theorem below
uses $X_0>0$.
lem-tamed-euler-uniform-moment-bounds:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $d,m\ge1$ be finite, $T>0$, and let $b,\sigma,\xi,W$ satisfy
the coefficient, Brownian, and initial-moment hypotheses of
[[thm-superlinear-sde-global-existence-and-moments]]. For each integer
$N\ge\max(1,\lceil T\rceil)$, put $h=T/N$ and define $Y_0,\ldots,Y_N$ by
[[alg-tamed-euler-superlinear-drift]]. Then for every finite $p\ge1$,
$$\sup_{N\ge\max(1,\lceil T\rceil)}\ \max_{0\le n\le N}\mathbb E|Y_n|^p<\infty.$$
The bound may depend on $p,T$, the coefficient constants, and the initial
moments, but not on $N$ or $n$.
thm-superlinear-sde-global-existence-and:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $d,m\ge1$ be finite, $T>0$, and let $W$ and $\xi$ satisfy
the filtered Brownian hypotheses in
[[def-locally-lipschitz-ito-sde-and-maximal-solution]] with $U=\mathbb R^d$.
Consider the autonomous SDE
$$dX_t=b(X_t)\,dt+\sigma(X_t)\,dW_t,\qquad X_0=\xi,$$
where $b\in C^1(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^d)$, $\sigma:\mathbb R^d\to
\mathbb R^{d\times m}$ is globally Lipschitz, and for constants $L,C<\infty$
and an integer $q\ge1$,
$$\langle x-y,b(x)-b(y)\rangle\le L|x-y|^2, \qquad \|Db(x)\|\le C(1+|x|^q).$$
Suppose $\mathbb E|\xi|^p<\infty$ for every finite $p\ge1$. Then the
maximal local strong solution is global on $[0,T]$, is unique up to
indistinguishability, and for every finite $p\ge1$,
$$\mathbb E\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t|^p<\infty.$$
The bound may depend on $p,T$, the coefficient constants, and the initial
moments. No global Lipschitz condition on the drift is assumed.
alg-drift-implicit-euler-sde:
## Definition

Assume AC and the Brownian conventions of
[[def-locally-lipschitz-ito-sde-and-maximal-solution]] on $[0,T]$ with
$U=\mathbb R^d$. The input is an autonomous continuous drift
$b:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$, a diffusion
$\sigma:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times m}$, an initial state $\xi$, and
$N\ge1$ with $h=T/N\le1$. Require a constant $\mu\ge0$ such that
$$\langle x-y,b(x)-b(y)\rangle\le-\mu|x-y|^2 \quad\text{for all }x,y\in\mathbb R^d.$$
The map $H_h(x)=x-hb(x)$ is bijective by
[[thm-backward-euler-dissipative-resolvent-contraction]]; write
$R_h=H_h^{-1}$. Return the grid values, step process, interpolation, and
status by these instructions.

1. If the input or dissipativity condition is invalid, return `invalid-input`.
2. Set $Y_0=\xi$. For $n=0,\ldots,N-1$, compute
$$u_n=Y_n+\sigma(Y_n)(W_{t_{n+1}}-W_{t_n}),\qquad Y_{n+1}=R_h(u_n).$$
3. In an exact-real implementation return `success`, the sequence, and the
piecewise-constant step process $\bar Y_t=Y_n$ on $[t_n,t_{n+1})$.
4. A finite numerical root solver may return `solve-failure` with the failed
index, its last iterate, and residual
$z-hb(z)-u_n$ if it cannot certify the unique root. That failed iterate is
not a scheme value and is not used in later steps; return the valid prefix
only.

For valid exact-real inputs every resolvent value exists uniquely and is
finite. A finite implementation failure therefore reports an unsuccessful
numerical solve, not a nonexistent mathematical root. The algorithm alone
makes no convergence or mean-square stability claim.
thm-cir-positive-solution-and-nonattainm:
## Statement

Assume AC and the Brownian conventions of
[[def-locally-lipschitz-ito-sde-and-maximal-solution]]. Let
$\kappa,\theta,\sigma>0$, let $x_0>0$ be deterministic, and suppose
$2\kappa\theta\ge\sigma^2$. Then the CIR SDE
$$dX_t=\kappa(\theta-X_t)dt+\sigma\sqrt{X_t}\,dW_t, \qquad X_0=x_0,$$
has a unique global strong solution on every finite horizon. Its paths remain
strictly positive and finite, and for every finite $p\ge1$,
$$\sup_{0\le t\le T}\mathbb E X_t^p<\infty.$$
No negative-moment bound or strong numerical convergence rate is asserted.
thm-tamed-euler-strong-order-half:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $d,m\ge1$, $T>0$, $b\in C^1(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^d)$,
and $\sigma:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times m}$ be globally Lipschitz.
Suppose constants $L,C<\infty$ and an integer $q\ge1$ satisfy
$$\langle x-y,b(x)-b(y)\rangle\le L|x-y|^2, \qquad \|Db(x)\|\le C(1+|x|^q).$$
Let $X$ be the unique strong solution of the corresponding autonomous SDE
from [[thm-superlinear-sde-global-existence-and-moments]], with initial state
$\xi$ having all finite moments. For $N\ge\max(1,\lceil T\rceil)$ put
$h=T/N$, and let $\widetilde Y$ be the continuous tamed Euler interpolation from
[[alg-tamed-euler-superlinear-drift]]. There is a constant $C_T$, independent
of $N$, such that
$$\mathbb E\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t-\widetilde Y_t|^2\le C_T h.$$
Thus the tamed Euler method has strong order one-half in the path-supremum
$L^2$ norm under the displayed hypotheses.
thm-cir-lamperti-scheme-converges-in-pro:
## Statement

Assume AC, $\kappa,\theta,\sigma>0$, $2\kappa\theta\ge\sigma^2$, and
deterministic $X_0=x_0>0$. Let $X$ be the positive CIR solution from
[[thm-cir-positive-solution-and-nonattainment]]. For $h=T/N$, initialize
$Z_0=\sqrt{x_0}$ and apply
[[alg-cir-lamperti-positive-implicit-scheme]] to obtain $Z_n$ and
$X_n^h=Z_n^2$. Then for every $T>0$,
$$\max_{0\le n\le N}|X_{t_n}-X_n^h|\longrightarrow0 \quad\text{in probability as }N\to\infty.$$
This is convergence in probability on each finite horizon; no $L^p$ error
rate is asserted.
thm-drift-implicit-euler-sde-strong-orde:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $d,m\ge1$ be finite, $T>0$, and consider the autonomous
SDE with $b\in C^1(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^d)$ and globally Lipschitz
$\sigma:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times m}$. Suppose that for constants
$\mu\ge0$, $C<\infty$, and an integer $q\ge1$,
$$\langle x-y,b(x)-b(y)\rangle\le-\mu|x-y|^2, \qquad \|Db(x)\|\le C(1+|x|^q).$$
Let $\xi$ have all finite moments and let $X$ be the corresponding global
strong solution. For $N\ge\max(1,\lceil T\rceil)$, put $h=T/N$ and let
$Y_n$ be the exact-resolvent drift-implicit Euler–Maruyama values from
[[alg-drift-implicit-euler-sde]]. There is a constant $C_T$ independent of
$N$ such that
$$\mathbb E\max_{0\le n\le N}|X_{t_n}-Y_n|^2\le C_T h.$$
Moreover, for two such numerical sequences driven by the same Brownian
increments but with initial values $\xi,\widetilde\xi$,
$$\mathbb E|Y_n-\widetilde Y_n|^2 \le e^{L_\sigma^2t_n}\mathbb E|\xi-\widetilde\xi|^2,$$
where $L_\sigma$ is a global Lipschitz constant of $\sigma$. The second
estimate is finite-time mean-square stability; it does not claim strict
contraction when diffusion is present.
cex-euler-moments-diverge-for-cubic-diss:
## Statement

Fix $T>0$ and consider
$$dX_t=-X_t^3dt+dW_t,\qquad X_0=0.$$
For $N\ge1$, let $h=T/N$ and let $Y_0=0$,
$$Y_{n+1}=Y_n-hY_n^3+(W_{t_{n+1}}-W_{t_n}),\qquad t_n=nh.$$
The exact solution has finite moments of every order at time $T$, but for
every $p\ge1$,
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb E|Y_N|^p=+\infty.$$
ex-cir-lamperti-scheme-positive-root-at-:
## Statement

Let $\kappa,\theta,\sigma,h>0$ satisfy $2\kappa\theta\ge\sigma^2$.
Starting the numerical Lamperti state at the boundary value $z_n=0$, even a
negative Brownian increment $\Delta W_n=-r$ with arbitrary $r\ge0$ gives a
strictly positive next state under the CIR scheme.
ex-noise-induced-instability-in-explicit:
## Statement

Consider the mean-square stable scalar SDE
$$dX_t=-2X_tdt+\sqrt3X_t\,dW_t,\qquad X_0=1.$$
Its exact second moment is $\mathbb E|X_t|^2=e^{-t}$. On a grid with
$h=1/2$, explicit Euler–Maruyama has one-step mean-square amplification
$3/2>1$, even though the deterministic Euler multiplier is zero. The
drift-implicit Euler–Maruyama update has one-step mean-square factor
$5/8<1$.
